column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, focusing on collaborative workflows between human developers and AI coding agents. Students learn to configure agent skills, tool use, and model context protocols to build reliable software environments. Through practical exercises, students construct executable specifications from natural language requirements and analyze agentic execution loops to debug operational failures. Additionally, they learn to design and assess AI-native software development workflows and evaluation pipelines against specific reliability requirements. The course is taught through three hours of lectures, one tutorial hour, and two practical lab hours per week over thirteen weeks, incorporating hands-on assignments and a collaborative software project. It is not a general introduction to machine learning, a traditional programming course, or a purely theoretical treatment of large language models. Instead, it emphasizes practical, workflow-oriented software engineering practices using emerging developer tools.

Course Code: Configure agent skills, tool use, and model context protocols for an AI-assisted development environment, using a supplied agent framework and API set, such that all public integration tests pass and no configuration warnings are reported.
column2: Construct executable specifications from a given natural language requirements document, using spec-driven development patterns, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column3: Analyse the operational loops of a software coding agent for a supplied buggy code repository, identifying at least three distinct failure causes in agentic execution, each supported by evidence from the execution logs.
column4: Assess an AI-native software development workflow and evaluation pipeline, for a given multi-component software project description, justifying each design decision against at least one stated reliability or automation requirement.

column2: Laboratory Exercise
Set up the local development environment, configure the AI coding agent framework, and parse configuration files to identify active components.
Implement a custom local file-search tool and register it with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to extend agent capabilities.
Configure and bind custom tools to a code-refactoring agent, ensuring the agent can invoke them correctly during local refactoring tasks.
Refine agent skills for complex refactoring tasks and translate a natural language use case into a structured specification template.
Construct executable specifications for an authentication module using spec-driven development patterns based on natural language requirements.
Generate automated test cases from the executable specifications constructed in the previous week and verify they execute without errors.
Open lab session for catch-up, debugging previous lab exercises, and mid-semester exam preparation. No new content is introduced.
Trace execution logs of a coding agent and analyze the tool-calling loop to identify state divergence during a failed file-write operation.
Debug state divergence in failed file operations by analyzing execution traces and correcting the agent's tool-calling parameters.
Set up and run an evaluation pipeline to compare the performance of two different AI-native software development workflows.
Design and implement a multi-component web application workflow using an AI-native software factory setup.
Assess and justify the reliability of the designed AI-native workflow against automation requirements, producing the final project deliverable.
Final project presentations and evaluation of the AI-native software development workflows.
